newsitem.title: USA: Japan watchful with flexible monetary policy-Kubo.
newsitem.headline: Japan watchful with flexible monetary policy-Kubo.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Sunday that Japan would take appropriate and flexible monetary policy while keeping careful watch over global economic conditions.
Kubo added that on the monetary side, Japan has maintained easy monetary policy by keeping its official discount rate at 0.5 percent since last September.
Japan's current account surplus has been diminishing steadily since 1993, with the first half of 1996 showing 34.5 percent drop from year ago same period, Kubo said.

He attributed this to changes in the nation's economic structure with manufacturers moving their production overseas and boost in imports with the deregulation of domestic markets. He stressed the need to tackle fiscal consolidation as public debt has mounted with past stimulus packages.
"We are at a stage where we must tackle fiscal reforms without delay with expected growth of the ageing population," he said in a statement.
Turning to industrilised countries, Kubo said they should place top priority on reducing state deficits, which hamper private-sector economies and can cause a shortage in global savings.
"I feel reassured that Europe and the United States are reducing their fiscal deficits ahead of us," he said.
Developing countries overall are continuing to show strong growth, Kubo added.

"I hope countries with new and emerging markets will come to contribute to continued growth in world economy by taking appropriate policies while watching out for overheating of their economies," Kubo said.
